   287→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   288→// Invite status check
   289→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   291→/**
   292→ * Check the status of an invite link (public, no auth required).
   293→ * The server returns only 'active' or 404 (to prevent token-existence

   295→ */
   296→export async function checkInviteStatus(token: string): Promise<'active' | 'expired'> {

   325→}

    14→/**

    28→  folderKey,
    29→  ipnsName,

    31→  isOpen,

    59→          setError('failed to load invite links');

   325→  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
   326→    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
   327→    sequenceNumber: newSeq,
   328→    entries: currentEntries,
   329→  };
   330→
   331→  // Non-blocking: folder delete already committed, bin is best-effort
   332→  try {
   333→    await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, userPublicKey, userPrivateKey });
   334→    store.setEntries(currentEntries, newSeq);
   335→  } catch {
   336→    console.error('[Bin] addManyToBin publish failed (non-blocking)');
   337→  }
   338→}

   340→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   341→// Public API: restoreFromBin
   342→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   343→
   344→/**
   345→ * Restore a bin entry to its original folder.
   346→ *
   347→ * Looks up the target folder by IPNS name. If found, re-adds the preserved
   348→ * FolderChild. Handles name collisions (appends " (restored)"). If original
   349→ * parent is also in the bin, attempts recursive parent restore (max depth 5).
   350→ * Falls back to root folder if parent is gone.
   351→ */
   352→export async function restoreFromBin(params: {
   353→  entryId: string;
   354→  userPublicKey: Uint8Array;
   355→  userPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
   356→}): Promise<void> {
   357→  return restoreFromBinInternal(params, 0);
   358→}
   359→
   360→async function restoreFromBinInternal(
   361→  params: { entryId: string; userPublicKey: Uint8Array; userPrivateKey: Uint8Array },
   362→  depth: number
   363→): Promise<void> {
   364→  const { entryId, userPublicKey, userPrivateKey } = params;
   365→
   366→  const binStore = useBinStore.getState();
   367→  const entry = binStore.entries.find((e) => e.id === entryId);
   368→  if (!entry) throw new Error('Bin entry not found');
   369→
   370→  // Resolve original parent folder
   371→  const targetFolder = await resolveTargetFolder(entry.originalParentIpnsName, depth, {
   372→    userPublicKey,
   373→    userPrivateKey,
   374→  });
   375→
   376→  // Get the FolderChild to restore
   377→  const child = getRestoredChild(entry);
   378→
   379→  // Check for name collisions in target folder and rename if needed
   380→  const finalChild = resolveNameCollision(child, targetFolder.children);
   381→
   382→  // Add child back to target folder
   383→  const { updateFolderMetadata } = await import('./folder.service');
   384→  const updatedChildren = [...targetFolder.children, finalChild];
   385→  const { newSequenceNumber } = await updateFolderMetadata({
   386→    folderId: targetFolder.id,
   387→    children: updatedChildren,
   388→    folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
   389→    ipnsPrivateKey: targetFolder.ipnsPrivateKey,
   390→    ipnsName: targetFolder.ipnsName,
   391→    sequenceNumber: targetFolder.sequenceNumber,
   392→  });
   393→
   394→  // Update folder store
   395→  const folderStore = useFolderStore.getState();
   396→  folderStore.updateFolderChildren(targetFolder.id, updatedChildren);
   397→  folderStore.updateFolderSequence(targetFolder.id, newSequenceNumber);
   398→
   399→  // If restoring a folder, re-add the folder node to the store
   400→  if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
   401→    const existingNode = folderStore.folders[entry.folderEntry.id];
   402→    if (!existingNode) {
   403→      // Create a placeholder node -- it will be fully loaded on next navigation
   404→      folderStore.setFolder({
   405→        id: entry.folderEntry.id,
   406→        name: finalChild.name,
   407→        ipnsName: entry.folderEntry.ipnsName,
   408→        parentId: targetFolder.id,
   409→        children: [],
   410→        isLoaded: false,
   411→        isLoading: false,
   412→        sequenceNumber: 0n,
   413→        // These will be populated when the folder is loaded
   414→        folderKey: new Uint8Array(32),
   415→        ipnsPrivateKey: new Uint8Array(64),
   416→      });
   417→    }
   418→  }
   419→
   420→  // Remove entry from bin metadata and publish
   421→  await removeEntriesFromBin([entryId], { userPublicKey, userPrivateKey });
   422→}
   423→
   424→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   425→// Public API: restoreFromBinBatch
   426→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   427→
   428→/**
   429→ * Restore multiple bin entries, publishing to the bin IPNS only once at the end.
   430→ *
   431→ * Each item is restored to its target folder (which may each require a folder
   432→ * publish), but the bin metadata is updated in a single publish.
   433→ */
   434→export async function restoreFromBinBatch(params: {
   435→  entryIds: string[];
   436→  userPublicKey: Uint8Array;
   437→  userPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
   438→}): Promise<void> {
   439→  const { entryIds, userPublicKey, userPrivateKey } = params;
   440→  if (entryIds.length === 0) return;
   441→
   442→  const { updateFolderMetadata } = await import('./folder.service');
   443→
   444→  const restoredIds: string[] = [];
   445→
   446→  for (const entryId of entryIds) {
   447→    // Read fresh state each iteration — recursive restores may mutate the store
   448→    const entry = useBinStore.getState().entries.find((e) => e.id === entryId);
   449→    if (!entry) continue;
   450→
   451→    try {
   452→      const targetFolder = await resolveTargetFolder(entry.originalParentIpnsName, 0, {
   453→        userPublicKey,
   454→        userPrivateKey,
   455→      });
   456→
   457→      const child = getRestoredChild(entry);
   458→      const finalChild = resolveNameCollision(child, targetFolder.children);
   459→
   460→      const updatedChildren = [...targetFolder.children, finalChild];
   461→      const { newSequenceNumber } = await updateFolderMetadata({
   462→        folderId: targetFolder.id,
   463→        children: updatedChildren,
   464→        folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
   465→        ipnsPrivateKey: targetFolder.ipnsPrivateKey,
   466→        ipnsName: targetFolder.ipnsName,
   467→        sequenceNumber: targetFolder.sequenceNumber,
   468→      });
   469→
   470→      const folderStore = useFolderStore.getState();
   471→      folderStore.updateFolderChildren(targetFolder.id, updatedChildren);
   472→      folderStore.updateFolderSequence(targetFolder.id, newSequenceNumber);
   473→
   474→      if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
   475→        const existingNode = folderStore.folders[entry.folderEntry.id];
   476→        if (!existingNode) {
   477→          folderStore.setFolder({
   478→            id: entry.folderEntry.id,
   479→            name: finalChild.name,
   480→            ipnsName: entry.folderEntry.ipnsName,
   481→            parentId: targetFolder.id,
   482→            children: [],
   483→            isLoaded: false,
   484→            isLoading: false,
   485→            sequenceNumber: 0n,
   486→            folderKey: new Uint8Array(32),
   487→            ipnsPrivateKey: new Uint8Array(64),
   488→          });
   489→        }
   490→      }
   491→
   492→      restoredIds.push(entryId);
   493→    } catch (err) {
   494→      console.error(`[Bin] Failed to restore entry ${entry.id}:`, err);
   495→    }
   496→  }
   497→
   498→  // Single bin IPNS publish for all restored entries
   499→  if (restoredIds.length > 0) {
   500→    await removeEntriesFromBin(restoredIds, { userPublicKey, userPrivateKey });
   501→  }
   502→}

   509→ * Permanently delete a bin entry: unpin CIDs and update quota.

   511→ * For files: resolves file IPNS -> gets CID -> unpins.

   514→export async function permanentlyDelete(params: {

   541→export async function permanentlyDeleteBatch(params: {

   617→export async function purgeExpired(params: {

   629→  if (expired.length === 0) return;

   647→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   650→
   651→/**
   652→ * Remove entries from bin metadata and publish the updated metadata.
   653→ */
   654→async function removeEntriesFromBin(
   655→  entryIds: string[],
   656→  params: { userPublicKey: Uint8Array; userPrivateKey: Uint8Array }
   657→): Promise<void> {
   658→  const binStore = useBinStore.getState();
   659→  const idsToRemove = new Set(entryIds);
   660→  const remainingEntries = binStore.entries.filter((e) => !idsToRemove.has(e.id));
   661→  const newSeq = binStore.sequenceNumber + 1;
   662→
   663→  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
   664→    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
   665→    sequenceNumber: newSeq,
   666→    entries: remainingEntries,
   667→  };
   668→
   669→  await saveBinMetadata({
   670→    metadata,
   671→    userPublicKey: params.userPublicKey,
   672→    userPrivateKey: params.userPrivateKey,
   673→  });
   674→
   675→  // Update local store (use setEntries with explicit seq to avoid double-increment)
   676→  binStore.setEntries(remainingEntries, newSeq);
   677→}
   678→
   679→/**
   680→ * Cleanup CIDs for a bin entry (unpin from IPFS + update quota).
   681→ *
   682→ * Files: use stored contentCid if available, else fall back to IPNS resolution.
   683→ * Folders: unwrap folderKey, decrypt folder metadata, decrypt each nested file's
   684→ * metadata to get CID for unpinning. Recurses for subfolders.
   685→ */
   686→async function cleanupEntryCids(entry: BinEntry, userPrivateKey: Uint8Array): Promise<void> {
   687→  if (entry.itemType === 'file') {
   688→    await unpinFileCids(entry);
   689→  } else if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
   690→    await cleanupFolderCids(entry.folderEntry, userPrivateKey);
   691→  }
   692→}
   693→
   694→/**
   695→ * Unpin a single file's content and metadata CIDs, and update quota.
   696→ *
   697→ * Prefers stored contentCid (captured at soft-delete time) to avoid
   698→ * re-decrypting encrypted file metadata (which was the GAP-1 bug).
   699→ * Falls back to legacy IPNS resolution for old entries without contentCid.
   700→ */
   701→async function unpinFileCids(entry: BinEntry): Promise<void> {
   702→  try {
   703→    // Preferred path: use stored contentCid from soft-delete time
   704→    if (entry.contentCid) {
   705→      await unpinFromIpfs(entry.contentCid);
   706→      if (Number.isFinite(entry.contentSize)) {
   707→        useQuotaStore.getState().removeUsage(entry.contentSize!);
   708→      }
   709→      // Unpin version CIDs captured at soft-delete time
   710→      if (entry.versionCids?.length) {
   711→        await unpinVersionCids({ versions: entry.versionCids });
   712→      }
   713→      // Also unpin the file metadata IPNS record CID
   714→      if (entry.filePointer) {
   715→        const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(entry.filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName);
   716→        if (resolved?.cid) {
   717→          await unpinFromIpfs(resolved.cid).catch(() => {});
   718→        }
   719→      }
   720→      return;
   721→    }
   722→
   723→    // Fallback for legacy entries without contentCid:
   724→    // Resolve IPNS and attempt to interpret file metadata as plaintext JSON.
   725→    // NOTE: For encrypted file metadata ({ iv, data }), JSON.parse will usually
   726→    // succeed, but the parsed object will not have cid/size, so no content unpin
   727→    // or quota reclaim happens (the original GAP-1 bug). Entries that hit this
   728→    // path may log an error but will not crash the delete flow.
   729→    if (!entry.filePointer) return;
   730→    const fileIpnsName = entry.filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName;
   731→    if (!fileIpnsName) return;
   732→
   733→    const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(fileIpnsName);
   734→    if (!resolved?.cid) return;
   735→
   736→    const metaBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(resolved.cid);
   737→    const metaJson = new TextDecoder().decode(metaBytes);
   738→    const fileMeta = JSON.parse(metaJson);
   739→
   740→    if (fileMeta.cid) {
   741→      await unpinFromIpfs(fileMeta.cid);
   742→      if (Number.isFinite(fileMeta.size)) {
   743→        useQuotaStore.getState().removeUsage(fileMeta.size);
   744→      }
   745→    }
   746→    await unpinVersionCids(fileMeta);
   747→
   748→    await unpinFromIpfs(resolved.cid).catch(() => {});
   749→  } catch (err) {
   750→    console.error(`[Bin] CID cleanup failed for file ${entry.id}:`, err);
   751→  }
   752→}
   753→
   754→/**
   755→ * Unpin version CIDs from a decrypted/parsed file metadata object and reclaim quota.
   756→ * Best-effort: errors on individual versions are caught and logged.
   757→ */
   758→async function unpinVersionCids(fileMeta: {
   759→  versions?: Array<{ cid?: string; size?: number }>;
   760→}): Promise<void> {
   761→  if (!Array.isArray(fileMeta.versions)) return;
   762→  for (const version of fileMeta.versions) {
   763→    try {
   764→      if (version.cid) {
   765→        await unpinFromIpfs(version.cid);
   766→      }
   767→      if (Number.isFinite(version.size)) {
   768→        useQuotaStore.getState().removeUsage(version.size!);
   769→      }
   770→    } catch {
   771→      // Best-effort for individual version cleanup
   772→    }
   773→  }
   774→}
   775→
   776→/**
   777→ * Recursively unpin all CIDs in a folder tree.
   778→ *
   779→ * Unwraps the folder's AES key using the user's private key, then decrypts
   780→ * the folder metadata to enumerate children. For each file child, decrypts
   781→ * the file metadata to extract the content CID for unpinning.
   782→ * For subfolder children, recurses with the user's private key.
   783→ */
   784→async function cleanupFolderCids(
   785→  folderEntry: FolderEntry,
   786→  userPrivateKey: Uint8Array
   787→): Promise<void> {
   788→  let folderMetadataCid: string | null = null;
   789→  try {
   790→    // Step 1: Unwrap the folder's AES key using user's private key (ECIES)
   791→    const wrappedFolderKey = hexToBytes(folderEntry.folderKeyEncrypted);
   792→    const folderKey = await unwrapKey(wrappedFolderKey, userPrivateKey);
   793→
   794→    // Step 2: Resolve folder's IPNS to get its metadata CID
   795→    const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(folderEntry.ipnsName);
   796→    if (!resolved?.cid) return;
   797→    folderMetadataCid = resolved.cid;
   798→
   799→    // Step 3: Fetch and decrypt the folder metadata
   800→    const metaBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(resolved.cid);
   801→    const metaJson = new TextDecoder().decode(metaBytes);
   802→    const encrypted = JSON.parse(metaJson) as EncryptedFolderMetadata;
   803→    const folderMeta = await decryptFolderMetadata(encrypted, folderKey);
   804→
   805→    // Step 4: For each child, unpin CIDs
   806→    for (const child of folderMeta.children) {
   807→      try {
   808→        if (child.type === 'file') {
   809→          const fp = child as FilePointer;
   810→          // Decrypt file metadata to get content CID
   811→          const fileResolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(fp.fileMetaIpnsName);
   812→          if (fileResolved?.cid) {
   813→            const fileMetaBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(fileResolved.cid);
   814→            const fileMetaJson = new TextDecoder().decode(fileMetaBytes);
   815→            const encryptedFileMeta = JSON.parse(fileMetaJson) as EncryptedFileMetadata;
   816→            const fileMeta = await decryptFileMetadata(encryptedFileMeta, folderKey);
   817→            if (fileMeta.cid) {
   818→              await unpinFromIpfs(fileMeta.cid);
   819→              if (Number.isFinite(fileMeta.size)) {
   820→                useQuotaStore.getState().removeUsage(fileMeta.size);
   821→              }
   822→            }
   823→            // Unpin any historical version CIDs
   824→            await unpinVersionCids(fileMeta);
   825→            // Also unpin the file metadata CID
   826→            await unpinFromIpfs(fileResolved.cid).catch(() => {});
   827→          }
   828→        } else if (child.type === 'folder') {
   829→          // Subfolder: folderKeyEncrypted is ECIES-wrapped with the user's publicKey
   830→          const subFe = child as FolderEntry;
   831→          await cleanupFolderCids(subFe, userPrivateKey);
   832→        }
   833→      } catch (childErr) {
   834→        console.error(`[Bin] Failed to cleanup CIDs for child ${child.name}:`, childErr);
   835→      }
   836→    }
   837→  } catch (err) {
   838→    console.error(`[Bin] Folder CID cleanup failed for ${folderEntry.ipnsName}:`, err);
   839→  } finally {
   840→    // Always unpin the folder metadata CID, even if child cleanup threw
   841→    if (folderMetadataCid) {
   842→      await unpinFromIpfs(folderMetadataCid).catch(() => {});
   843→    }
   844→  }
   845→}
   846→
   847→/**
   848→ * Resolve the target folder for a restore operation.
   849→ *
   850→ * Walks the folder store to find a folder with the given IPNS name.
   851→ * If not found, checks if the parent is in the bin (recursive restore).
   852→ * Falls back to root folder.
   853→ */
   854→async function resolveTargetFolder(
   855→  parentIpnsName: string,
   856→  depth: number,
   857→  params: { userPublicKey: Uint8Array; userPrivateKey: Uint8Array }
   858→): Promise<FolderNode> {
   859→  // Max recursion depth to prevent infinite loops
   860→  if (depth > 5) {
   861→    console.warn('[Bin] Max restore depth reached, falling back to root');
   862→    return getRootFolder();
   863→  }
   864→
   865→  // Look up folder by IPNS name in folder store
   866→  const folders = useFolderStore.getState().folders;
   867→  const targetFolder = Object.values(folders).find((f) => f.ipnsName === parentIpnsName);
   868→
   869→  if (targetFolder) {
   870→    return targetFolder;
   871→  }
   872→
   873→  // Check if parent is in the bin
   874→  const binStore = useBinStore.getState();
   875→  const parentBinEntry = binStore.entries.find(
   876→    (e) => e.itemType === 'folder' && e.folderEntry && e.folderEntry.ipnsName === parentIpnsName
   877→  );
   878→
   879→  if (parentBinEntry) {
   880→    // Restore parent first (recursive, depth incremented)
   881→    console.log(`[Bin] Restoring parent folder (id: ${parentBinEntry.id}) first`);
   882→    await restoreFromBinInternal(
   883→      {
   884→        entryId: parentBinEntry.id,
   885→        userPublicKey: params.userPublicKey,
   886→        userPrivateKey: params.userPrivateKey,
   887→      },
   888→      depth + 1
   889→    );
   890→
   891→    // After restoring parent, try to find it again
   892→    const updatedFolders = useFolderStore.getState().folders;
   893→    const restoredParent = Object.values(updatedFolders).find((f) => f.ipnsName === parentIpnsName);
   894→    if (restoredParent) {
   895→      return restoredParent;
   896→    }
   897→  }
   898→
   899→  // Parent truly gone -- restore to root
   900→  console.warn(`[Bin] Original parent not found (${parentIpnsName}), restoring to root`);
   901→  return getRootFolder();
   902→}
   903→
   904→/**
   905→ * Get the root folder from the folder store.
   906→ */
   907→function getRootFolder(): FolderNode {
   908→  const folders = useFolderStore.getState().folders;

     8→import {

    20→import type { PublishIpnsEntryDtoRecordType } from '../api/models/publishIpnsEntryDtoRecordType';

    22→/**
    23→ * Create an IPNS record locally and publish via backend.
    24→ *
    25→ * The record is signed locally using the Ed25519 private key, then
    26→ * the backend relays it to the IPFS network via delegated routing.
    27→ *
    28→ * @param params.ipnsPrivateKey - Ed25519 private key (64 bytes in libp2p format)
    29→ * @param params.ipnsName - IPNS name (k51.../bafzaa... format)
    30→ * @param params.metadataCid - CID of the encrypted metadata blob
    31→ * @param params.sequenceNumber - Current sequence number (will be incremented before publish)
    32→ * @param params.encryptedIpnsPrivateKey - Hex ECIES-wrapped key for TEE (first publish only)
    33→ * @param params.keyEpoch - TEE key epoch (required with encryptedIpnsPrivateKey)
    34→ * @param params.expectedSequenceNumber - Pre-increment sequence number for conflict detection (folder records only)
    35→ */
    36→export async function createAndPublishIpnsRecord(params: {
    37→  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
    38→  ipnsName: string;
    39→  metadataCid: string;
    40→  sequenceNumber: bigint;
    41→  encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string;
    42→  keyEpoch?: number;
    43→  expectedSequenceNumber?: string;
    44→}): Promise<{ success: boolean; sequenceNumber: bigint }> {
    45→  // 1. Create IPNS record pointing to /ipfs/{metadataCid}
    46→  // 24 hour lifetime (will be republished by TEE every 3 hours)
    47→  const record = await createIpnsRecord(
    48→    params.ipnsPrivateKey,
    49→    `/ipfs/${params.metadataCid}`,
    50→    params.sequenceNumber,
    51→    24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 // 24 hours in ms
    52→  );
    53→
    54→  // 2. Marshal to bytes for transport
    55→  const recordBytes = marshalIpnsRecord(record);
    56→
    57→  // 3. Base64 encode for API transmission
    58→  const recordBase64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...recordBytes));
    59→
    60→  // 4. Call backend API to relay to IPFS network
    61→  const response = await ipnsControllerPublishRecord({
    62→    ipnsName: params.ipnsName,
    63→    record: recordBase64,
    64→    metadataCid: params.metadataCid,
    65→    encryptedIpnsPrivateKey: params.encryptedIpnsPrivateKey,
    66→    keyEpoch: params.keyEpoch,
    67→    expectedSequenceNumber: params.expectedSequenceNumber,
    68→  });
    69→
    70→  return {
    71→    success: response.success,
    72→    sequenceNumber: BigInt(response.sequenceNumber),
    73→  };
    74→}
    75→
    76→/**
    77→ * Batch publish multiple IPNS records in a single API call.
    78→ *
    79→ * Sends all records (folder and/or file) to the batch endpoint,

    82→ *
    83→ * @param records - Array of IPNS record payloads to publish

    88→    ipnsName: string;

   104→      keyEpoch: r.keyEpoch,
   105→      recordType: r.recordType as PublishIpnsEntryDtoRecordType | undefined,
   106→      expectedSequenceNumber: r.expectedSequenceNumber,

   108→  });

   111→    totalSucceeded: response.totalSucceeded,
   112→    totalFailed: response.totalFailed,
   113→  };
   114→}

   116→/**
   117→ * Verify the Ed25519 signature on an IPNS record.
   118→ * Per IPFS spec, the signature is over "ipns-signature:" + cborData.
   119→ *
   120→ * @param signatureV2 - base64 Ed25519 signature (64 bytes)
   121→ * @param data - base64 CBOR data that was signed
   122→ * @param pubKey - base64 raw Ed25519 public key (32 bytes)
   123→ * @returns true if valid
   124→ */
   125→export async function verifyIpnsSignature(
   126→  signatureV2: string,
   127→  data: string,
   128→  pubKey: string
   129→): Promise<boolean> {
   130→  const sigBytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(signatureV2), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));

   133→
   134→  // Per IPFS IPNS spec, signature is over "ipns-signature:" + cborData
   135→  const signedData = concatBytes(IPNS_SIGNATURE_PREFIX, dataBytes);
   136→  return verifyEd25519(sigBytes, signedData, pubKeyBytes);

### E2E Flows

**Broken:** 0 flows have breaks

### Detailed Findings

---

#### 1. Identity Chain: Core Kit -> SIWE -> MFA -> Deterministic IPNS (CONNECTED)

**Trace:**
- `/apps/api/src/auth/controllers/identity.controller.ts` provides three identity endpoints: Google (`/auth/identity/google`), Email OTP (`/auth/identity/email/verify-otp`), and Wallet SIWE (`/auth/identity/wallet`)
- Each endpoint calls `SiweService.hashIdentifier()` or `hashWalletAddress()` for SHA-256 based identity resolution, then `JwtIssuerService.signIdentityJwt()` to issue a CipherBox JWT
- `/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts` imports `useCoreKitAuth` from `lib/web3auth/hooks` which sends the CipherBox JWT to Core Kit's `loginWithJWT`
- On REQUIRED_SHARE (MFA needed): `useAuth` sets `pendingAuthMethod` and calls `authApi.login` with placeholder `pending-core-kit-{userId}` publicKey for temporary scoped access
- `/apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts` lines 68-101 handle placeholder resolution -- both first-login completion (scenario A) and REQUIRED_SHARE temp auth (scenario B, lookup by userId from JWT sub)
- `useMfa.ts` imports `useCoreKit` and calls `coreKit.enableMFA()`, `coreKit.inputFactorKey()`, `coreKit.createFactor()` -- all Web3Auth MPC Core Kit operations
- `useDeviceApproval.ts` imports `useMfa.inputFactorKey` and `useAuth.completeRequiredShare` -- the full cross-device approval chain is wired: bulletin board poll -> ECIES decrypt factor key -> `inputFactorKey` -> `completeRequiredShare` -> `completeBackendAuth`
- IPNS derivation: `@cipherbox/crypto` exports `deriveIpnsName`, `deriveBinIpnsKeypair`, `deriveRegistryIpnsKeypair`, `deriveFileIpnsKeypair` -- all deterministic from user keys

**Verdict:** Fully connected. The identity chain from login through MFA through deterministic IPNS derivation is sound.

---

#### 2. Desktop Catch-Up Chain: Windows -> macOS -> v1 Removal -> Linux -> Cross-Platform E2E (CONNECTED)

**Trace:**
- `/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/` has platform-conditional compilation: `#[cfg(feature = "fuse")]` for macOS/Linux, `#[cfg(feature = "winfsp")]` for Windows
- Both platforms share: `InodeTable`, `MetadataCache`, `ContentCache`, `FileHandle`, `PublishCoordinator`
- macOS `operations.rs` and Windows `windows/operations.rs` both implement FUSE callbacks with the same patterns
- Both platforms handle 409 conflicts via `PublishResult::Conflict` -- macOS `mod.rs` lines 299-458, Windows `windows/write_ops.rs` lines 192-213
- Desktop FUSE creates `BinEntry` on file/folder delete: macOS `write_ops.rs` line 367, Windows `windows/write_ops.rs` line 633
- Desktop publishes bin entries to IPNS: `fuse/mod.rs` lines 475-581 (`add_bin_entry` function with full encrypt/publish cycle)
- Cross-platform E2E scripts: `/tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/` has paired `.sh` and `.ps1` scripts for `run-all`, `test-fuse-operations`, `test-round-trip`, `test-recycle-bin`, `test-conflict-detection`
- v2 metadata: Both macOS and Windows write `"version": "v2"` in folder metadata (write_ops.rs line 491)

**Verdict:** Fully connected. All three platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) share core data structures and have platform-specific FUSE implementations.

---

#### 3. Per-File IPNS -> Desktop (CONNECTED)

**Trace:**
- `@cipherbox/crypto` exports `deriveFileIpnsKeypair`, `generateFileIpnsKeypair`, `encryptFileMetadata`, `decryptFileMetadata`, `FilePointer` type
- Web: `file-metadata.service.ts` uses these for creating, resolving, and updating per-file IPNS records
- Desktop Rust: `crypto/folder.rs` defines `FilePointer` with `file_meta_ipns_name` field; FUSE read operations resolve per-file IPNS to fetch file metadata and content CID
- Desktop `operations.rs` line 284-299: Per-file IPNS publishes do NOT use conflict detection (correct -- file metadata has its own IPNS keypair, no multi-device contention on same file record)

**Verdict:** Fully connected. Per-file IPNS is supported in both web and desktop.

---

#### 4. Sharing -> Link Sharing (CONNECTED)

**Trace:**
- **Phase 14 (User-to-User):** `shares.controller.ts` provides CRUD, `share.service.ts` wraps the Orval client, `ShareDialog.tsx` renders the share UI with tab bar
- **Phase 15 (Link Sharing):** Two controllers: `ShareInvitesController` at `/shares/invites` (authenticated management) and `InvitesController` at `/invites` (public + authenticated claim)
- `invite.service.ts` generates ephemeral keypair, wraps item key with ephemeral pubkey, calls `shareInvitesControllerCreateInvite`, builds URL with ephemeral private key in hash fragment
- `InvitePage.tsx` reads token from route params and ephemeral key from `searchParams.get('key')`, checks status, renders auth UI, auto-claims on `isAuthenticated` change
- Claim flow: `claimInvite()` fetches full invite data, unwraps with ephemeral key, re-wraps with user's own pubkey, POSTs re-wrapped keys to `/invites/:token/claim`
- Server `share-invite.service.ts` `claimInvite()` creates standard Phase 14 `Share` + `ShareKey` records -- reusing existing sharing infrastructure
- **Post-share mutations:** `share.service.ts` `reWrapForRecipients()` is called after upload/folder creation to propagate keys to all share recipients
- **Lazy key rotation:** `share.service.ts` `executeLazyRotation()` generates new folder key, re-wraps for remaining recipients, hard-deletes revoked shares

**Verdict:** Fully connected. Link sharing builds on top of user-to-user sharing. The invite lifecycle (create -> claim -> share) is complete.

#### 5. Phase 15 Invite Revoke Bug Status (FIXED)

**Trace of the full revoke chain:**
1. `InviteLinkTab.tsx` line 120: `handleRevoke(inviteId)` receives `invite.id` (UUID from API response, line 198: `key={invite.id}`)
2. `invite.service.ts` line 331: `revokeInvite(inviteId)` calls `shareInvitesControllerRevokeInvite(inviteId)`
3. Generated API client `/apps/web/src/api/share-invites/share-invites.ts` line 249: sends `DELETE /shares/invites/${inviteId}`
4. `ShareInvitesController.revokeInvite()` receives `inviteId` via `@Param('inviteId', ParseUUIDPipe)` -- validates UUID format
5. `ShareInviteService.revokeInvite(inviteId, sharerId)` line 248: `findOne({ where: { id: inviteId } })` -- looks up by primary key UUID

The original bug was passing the invite `token` (base64url string) where the `inviteId` (UUID) was expected. The current code consistently uses `invite.id` (UUID) throughout. The `ParseUUIDPipe` would reject a base64url token with a 400 Bad Request, providing defense-in-depth. **Status: FIXED.**

#### 6. Recycle Bin -> CID Unpinning (CONNECTED)

**Trace:**
- `bin.service.ts` `permanentlyDelete()` calls `cleanupEntryCids()` which:
  - For files: uses `entry.contentCid` (captured at soft-delete time) to call `unpinFromIpfs()`, plus unpins version CIDs from `entry.versionCids`
  - For folders: recursively decrypts folder metadata, resolves each child file's metadata, unpins all content and metadata CIDs
  - Updates `useQuotaStore` with `removeUsage()` for quota reclamation
- Phase 17.1 fix: `enrichBinEntryWithFileMetadata()` (bin.service.ts line 183) resolves file metadata at soft-delete time, capturing `contentCid`, `contentSize`, and `versionCids` directly on the `BinEntry` -- this was the GAP-1 fix
- Desktop Rust: `fuse/write_ops.rs` lines 280-381 build `BinEntry` with `content_cid`, `content_size`, and `version_cids` from file metadata, matching the web pattern
- Windows: `fuse/windows/write_ops.rs` lines 633-649 similarly captures CID data in `BinEntry`

**Verdict:** Fully connected. CID unpinning is integrated for both web and desktop permanent deletes.

**Trace:**
- **API:** `ipns.controller.ts` returns 409 with `currentSequenceNumber` when `expectedSequenceNumber` mismatches (line 61, 103)

# Requirements: CipherBox

**Defined:** 2026-01-20
**Core Value:** Zero-knowledge privacy - files encrypted client-side, server never sees plaintext

## v1 Requirements

Requirements for initial release. Each maps to roadmap phases.

### Authentication

- [x] **AUTH-01**: User can sign up with email and password via Web3Auth
- [x] **AUTH-02**: User can sign in with OAuth (Google, Apple, GitHub) via Web3Auth
- [x] **AUTH-03**: User can sign in with magic link (passwordless email) via Web3Auth
- [x] **AUTH-04**: User can sign in with external wallet (MetaMask, WalletConnect) via Web3Auth
- [x] **AUTH-05**: User session persists via access token (15min) and refresh token (7 days)
- [x] **AUTH-06**: User can link multiple auth methods to the same vault
- [x] **AUTH-07**: User can log out and all keys are cleared from memory

### Encryption

- [x] **CRYPT-01**: Files are encrypted client-side with AES-256-GCM before upload
- [x] **CRYPT-02**: File keys are wrapped with user's public key via ECIES (secp256k1)
- [x] **CRYPT-03**: Folder metadata is encrypted with folder key (AES-256-GCM)
- [x] **CRYPT-04**: IPNS records are signed client-side with Ed25519 keys
- [x] **CRYPT-05**: Private key exists only in client RAM, never persisted or transmitted
- [x] **CRYPT-06**: Each file uses unique random key and IV (no deduplication)

### File Operations

- [x] **FILE-01**: User can upload files up to 100MB
- [x] **FILE-02**: User can download and decrypt files
- [x] **FILE-03**: User can delete files (with IPFS unpin)
- [x] **FILE-04**: User can rename files
- [x] **FILE-05**: User can move files between folders
- [x] **FILE-06**: User can select multiple files for bulk upload
- [x] **FILE-07**: User can select multiple files for bulk delete

### Folder Operations

- [x] **FOLD-01**: User can create folders
- [x] **FOLD-02**: User can delete folders (recursive)
- [x] **FOLD-03**: User can nest folders up to 20 levels deep
- [x] **FOLD-04**: User can rename folders
- [x] **FOLD-05**: User can move folders between parent folders
- [x] **FOLD-06**: Each folder has its own IPNS keypair for metadata

### Backend API

- [x] **API-01**: Backend verifies Web3Auth JWT via JWKS endpoint

   172→**File:** `apps/web/src/services/bin.service.ts` lines 648-668
   173→
   174→**Problem:** `unpinFileCids()` fetches file metadata from IPFS and parses it as plain JSON, expecting `{ cid, size }`. However, file metadata is AES-256-GCM encrypted via `encryptFileMetadata()` -- the IPFS blob is `{ iv: "hex...", data: "base64..." }`, not a plain FileMetadata object.

   183→- (b) Store plaintext CID + size in `BinEntry` at soft-delete time (simpler, lower risk)

### NEW Integration Gaps

#### GAP-1 (CRITICAL): Bin permanent delete cannot unpin file CIDs

**File:** `apps/web/src/services/bin.service.ts` lines 648-668

**Problem:** `unpinFileCids()` fetches file metadata from IPFS and parses it as plain JSON, expecting `{ cid, size }`. However, file metadata is AES-256-GCM encrypted via `encryptFileMetadata()` -- the IPFS blob is `{ iv: "hex...", data: "base64..." }`, not a plain FileMetadata object.

**Impact:** When permanently deleting from bin, CIDs are **never unpinned**. `removeUsage()` never executes because `fileMeta.cid` is always undefined. Affects `permanentlyDelete`, `emptyBin`, and `purgeExpired` -- all three permanent-delete paths.

**Root cause:** The bin stores `FilePointer` (which has `fileMetaIpnsName`) but NOT the `folderKey` needed to decrypt the file metadata. At permanent-delete time, the parent folder may already be deleted.

**Fix options:**

- (a) Store `folderKey` (ECIES-wrapped) in `BinEntry` at soft-delete time
- (b) Store plaintext CID + size in `BinEntry` at soft-delete time (simpler, lower risk)
- (c) Walk folder tree to recover `folderKey` if parent exists

#### GAP-2 (MODERATE): Windows desktop delete skips recycle bin

**File:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/write_ops.rs` line 480+

**Problem:** macOS/Linux FUSE `handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir` call `spawn_bin_entry_publish()` to create bin entries on delete. The Windows WinFsp `handle_cleanup` with `FspCleanupDelete` flag does NOT call `spawn_bin_entry_publish()`.

**Impact:** Files deleted via Windows desktop go straight to permanent deletion without bin protection. macOS/Linux users get recycle bin; Windows users do not.

**Evidence:** `grep -r "bin_entry\|spawn_bin_entry_publish" apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/` returns no matches.

### NEW Integration Gaps

#### GAP-1 (CRITICAL): Bin permanent delete cannot unpin file CIDs

**File:** `apps/web/src/services/bin.service.ts` lines 648-668

**Problem:** `unpinFileCids()` fetches file metadata from IPFS and parses it as plain JSON, expecting `{ cid, size }`. However, file metadata is AES-256-GCM encrypted via `encryptFileMetadata()` -- the IPFS blob is `{ iv: "hex...", data: "base64..." }`, not a plain FileMetadata object.

**Root cause:** The bin stores `FilePointer` (which has `fileMetaIpnsName`) but NOT the `folderKey` needed to decrypt the file metadata. At permanent-delete time, the parent folder may already be deleted.

**Fix options:**

- (a) Store `folderKey` (ECIES-wrapped) in `BinEntry` at soft-delete time
- (b) Store plaintext CID + size in `BinEntry` at soft-delete time (simpler, lower risk)
- (c) Walk folder tree to recover `folderKey` if parent exists

**Impact:** Files deleted via Windows desktop go straight to permanent deletion without bin protection. macOS/Linux users get recycle bin; Windows users do not.

**Evidence:** `grep -r "bin_entry\|spawn_bin_entry_publish" apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/` returns no matches.

# CipherBox v1.0 Production Milestone 2 Audit

**Initial audit:** 2026-03-04
**Re-audited:** 2026-03-05 (post Phase 17.1 gap closure + Phase 12 verification + integration checker)
**Status:** TECH DEBT (all requirements met, no critical blockers, 9 low-priority items)

## Executive Summary

All 28 actionable M2 requirements are satisfied across 20 phases. Two requirements (SYNC-05, SYNC-06) and one TEE requirement (TEE-06) were explicitly deferred to M3. All previously identified critical and moderate gaps have been closed by Phase 17.1 and subsequent fixes.

**Previous audit (2026-03-04) found 2 critical integration gaps:**
1. ~~Bin permanent delete cannot unpin file CIDs~~ → FIXED in Phase 17.1
2. ~~Windows desktop delete skips recycle bin~~ → FIXED in Phase 17.1

**This audit confirms:** All gaps closed. 38/38 cross-phase connections verified. 8/8 E2E flows complete. TypeScript compiles clean on both web and API.

## Requirements Coverage

### Satisfied (28/30)

| Requirement | Description | Phase | Status |
|-------------|-------------|-------|--------|
| SHARE-01 | Folder sharing via ECIES re-wrapping | 14 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-02 | Share by pasting recipient's public key | 14 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-03 | Instant share on public key paste | 14 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-04 | Revoke share with lazy key rotation | 14 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-05 | "Shared with me" browser at ~/shared | 14 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-06 | Shareable link with decryption key in URL fragment | 15 | SATISFIED |
| SHARE-07 | Link claim requires auth, auto-claims on login | 15 | SATISFIED |
| SRCH-01 | Client-side file name search across all folders | 15.1 | SATISFIED |
| SRCH-02 | Encrypted search index in IndexedDB | 15.1 | SATISFIED |
| SRCH-03 | Incremental index update on IPNS change | 15.1 | SATISFIED |
| MFA-01 | MFA enrollment via Web3Auth settings | 12.4 | SATISFIED |
| MFA-02 | Device share as MFA factor | 12.4 | SATISFIED |
| MFA-03 | Backup recovery phrase | 12.4 | SATISFIED |
| MFA-04 | MFA enrollment preserves keypair | 12.4 | SATISFIED |
| VER-01 | Auto-retain previous file versions | 13 | SATISFIED |
| VER-02 | View version history | 13 | SATISFIED |
| VER-03 | Restore previous version | 13 | SATISFIED |
| VER-04 | Retention policy (max 10 versions) | 13 | SATISFIED |
| VER-05 | Version storage counted against quota | 13 | SATISFIED |
| BIN-01 | Soft-delete to recycle bin | 17 | SATISFIED |
| BIN-02 | Browse and restore bin items | 17 | SATISFIED |
| BIN-03 | Permanent delete unpins CIDs + reclaims quota | 17.1 | SATISFIED |
| BIN-04 | Auto-purge after retention period | 17 | SATISFIED |
| BIN-05 | Bin items count against quota, emptying reclaims | 17.1 | SATISFIED |
| SYNC-04 | Conflict detection via sequence number mismatch | 16 | SATISFIED |
| PLAT-01 | Linux desktop app with FUSE mount | 11.3 | SATISFIED |
| PLAT-02 | Windows desktop app with WinFsp | 11 | SATISFIED |
| E2E-01 through E2E-05 | Cross-platform E2E testing | 11.4 | SATISFIED |

### Deferred to M3 (2 requirements + 1 TEE)

| Requirement | Description | Rationale |
|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| SYNC-05 | Offline write queue with retry | Conflict detection (SYNC-04) delivers core value; queue adds complexity for M3 |
| SYNC-06 | Idempotency keys for queued ops | Depends on SYNC-05 |
| TEE-06 | AWS Nitro fallback TEE provider | Phase 22 in M3 roadmap |

## Cross-Phase Integration

**Integration checker verified 38 key connections. 0 gaps. 0 orphaned exports.**

### Key Connections Verified

|------------|--------|
| Identity chain: Core Kit → SIWE → MFA → deterministic IPNS | CONNECTED |
| Desktop chain: Windows → macOS catch-up → v1 removal → Linux → E2E | CONNECTED |
| Per-file IPNS → Desktop FUSE (macOS/Windows/Linux) | CONNECTED |
| User-to-user sharing → Link sharing (invite reuses Share records) | CONNECTED |
| Recycle bin → CID unpinning on permanent delete (web + desktop) | CONNECTED |
| Advanced sync (409 conflict) → All folder mutations (web + desktop) | CONNECTED |
| Search index → Folder metadata with sync-triggered rebuild | CONNECTED |
| Auth protection → All sensitive routes (4/4 protected) | CONNECTED |
| Logout → Store cleanup (12 stores + file size cache via clearAllUserStores) | CONNECTED |

- `apps/api`: `tsc --noEmit` exit code 0

| Link sharing (create invite → claim → folder invite → revoke) | `invite-link-workflow.spec.ts` | Complete |
